question: ploidy
answer: 2 haplotype copies of each of 16 chromosome numbers; an older duplication shows on part of the genome (15% of the genome in homeolog blocks), too little to read duplicated sets from.
evidence: copies from the assembly (2 per number); 15% of the genome in homeolog blocks

question: origin_like_structure
answer: Not assessable: duplicated blocks are detected (homeology map), but no whole-chromosome homeolog pairs to read the copies across.
evidence: homeology map: 15% of the genome in blocks, 7 chromosome pairs; no whole-chromosome pairs

question: te_markers
answer: Only the absolute marker fraction is available (two copies per number); it does not separate diploid, auto- and allopolyploid, so no reading is made from it.

question: rediploidization
answer: Advanced: no stretch where homeologs are as close as alleles, and the karyotype has been rearranged since the duplication. Also: 2 chromosome(s) carry blocks homeologous to two or more others (chr06:chr07+chr14, chr07:chr06+chr16): fusions, fissions or translocations since the duplication.
evidence: residual tetrasomy on 0/12 homeolog-paired chromosome numbers; homeology map: 15% of the genome in 22 homeolog blocks, 7 chromosome pairs, block-divergence CV 0.14
